title: Random forest questionnaire classifier aids diagnosis of transient loss of consciousness
summary: In 178 prospectively recruited patients with transient loss of consciousness, a random forest trained on nine patient questionnaire items correctly identified 63 of 78 diagnoses (80.8%, 95% CI 70.0-88.5) in an independent validation sample, versus 70.5% for assessing clinicians. Diagnoses were set by two expert raters after 6 months of follow-up. Witness recruitment was low so the model uses patient answers only, the validation sample is small and sensitivity was low for some diagnoses.
ai_technology: Random forest classifier on patient questionnaire responses, compared with penalized linear regression and referrer diagnosis
organization: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; University of Sheffield

evidence.tested: Independent development and validation samples from prospectively recruited patients; 6-month expert-rated reference diagnosis. Classified as retrospective or benchmark because the model was not shown to be tested as a frozen model in new clinical use.
evidence.unknown: Use in routine assessment, performance for low-sensitivity diagnoses and results with witness data; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts the cause of transient loss of consciousness from questionnaire answers.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref. Full text not accessed.
